extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service staff, conservation scientists, land managers, and interested stakeholders (e.g., NGOs, regulated parties, Tribes)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and analytical criteria used by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to evaluate whether a listed species should be removed from the Federal Lists of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants, and the related procedural and monitoring requirements for delisting. Includes threat analysis, species-status assessment, peer review, public comment response, and post-delisting monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-factor analysis under the Act (Factors A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Act, we may determine that a species is an endangered species or a threatened species because of any of five factors: (A) The present or threatened destruction, modification, or curtailment of its habitat or range; (B) overutilization for commercial, recreational, scientific, or educational purposes; (C) disease or predation; (D) the inadequacy of existing regulatory mechanisms; and (E) other natural or manmade factors affecting its continued existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination to list, delist, or reclassify must be based on analysis of these factors. Threats should be evaluated for their effects on individuals, populations (analysis units/AUs), and the species as a whole, and considered in cumulative context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delisting reasons per 50 CFR 424.11(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our regulations at 50 CFR 424.11(e) identify four reasons why a species might be delisted: (1) The species is extinct; (2) the species has recovered to the point it no longer meets the definition of endangered or threatened; (3) new information shows the listed entity does not meet the definition of an endangered or threatened species; or (4) new information shows the listed entity does not meet the definition of a species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A final delisting determination must clearly identify which regulatory reason applies and support that finding with the best available scientific and commercial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the best available scientific and commercial data
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination must be made on the basis of the best available scientific and commercial data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile and rely on peer-reviewed studies, SSA reports, agency technical notes, monitoring data, and other credible sources. Where multiple estimates exist, justify choices (e.g., conservative use of lower confidence limits). Document data sources and make supporting materials publicly available (e.g., regulations.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Species Status Assessment (SSA) requirement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: An SSA team prepares an SSA report to inform status reviews and listing/delisting decisions; the SSA compiles the best scientific and commercial data concerning species' status, including impacts of past, present, and future factors (negative and beneficial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSA is the foundation for proposed and final rules; it should evaluate current condition and plausible future scenarios, analyze threats and cumulative effects, and provide metrics used in the viability evaluation (e.g., resiliency, redundancy, representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review of SSA and incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with the Service's peer review policy, independent scientific review of information in SSA reports is solicited and appropriate results are incorporated into the SSA and rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document peer review solicitation and responses; include summaries of peer review comments and responses in the proposed/final rule; maintain peer reviewer identities and comments as public records (when appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resiliency, redundancy, and representation (RRR) viability framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate species viability using levels of resiliency (ability of populations to withstand variation), redundancy (multiple populations/AUs to reduce extinction risk), and representation (genetic/ecological diversity across environmental gradients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess current RRR and project for plausible future scenarios; use RRR results to decide if species meets the ESA definitions of endangered or threatened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical Framework: scale of effect (individual vs. AU vs. species)
rubrics_metrics.description: Threats are assessed at individual, population (analysis unit, AU), and species levels; only threats with the potential to produce AU- or species-level effects are included in the resiliency analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document rationale when excluding localized/individual-level impacts from species-level analyses. Evaluate expected species response to threats, actions that ameliorate threats, and cumulative effects across scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of cumulative effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The SSA/analysis must evaluate the cumulative impact of multiple stressors (e.g., livestock grazing, invasive species, oil and gas development, OHV use, utility corridors, climate change) on the species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integrated scenarios and modeling to assess combined effects; explain how cumulative impacts influence resiliency, redundancy, and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of plausible future scenarios (optimistic/realistic/pessimistic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project species' condition under multiple plausible future scenarios (including pessimistic) to evaluate future resiliency, redundancy, and representation through the foreseeable future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe scenario assumptions (e.g., increases in stressors, regulatory changes), and report how outcomes vary across scenarios to support a delisting conclusion only when the species is expected to remain secure across plausible futures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population estimate standards and conservative use of minimum estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple population estimates exist, the Service may use conservative metrics (e.g., the 90 percent lower confidence limit) as better reflections of minimum population size; adopt peer-reviewed sampling methods (macroplots with randomly selected transects) and prefer systematic, peer-reviewed, rangewide methods over opportunistic counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain sampling methodology, justify why chosen estimates are reliable/best available, and explain conservatism (e.g., lower confidence bound) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criteria for threats in resiliency analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Only threats that have the potential to cause AU- or species-level effects (i.e., measurable impacts on population-level viability) are included in the resiliency evaluation; threats confined to individual plants are generally excluded from species-level resiliency scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document assessment of each threat's magnitude and scale; provide references supporting inclusion/exclusion decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of adequacy and persistence of conservation and regulatory mechanisms (Factor D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate existing conservation efforts and regulatory mechanisms (e.g., BLM sensitive species protections, ACECs, CITES) and whether those mechanisms will continue to limit threats post-delisting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the durability and expected enforcement of non-ESA protections and incorporate them into future scenario analyses; clearly state when protections will cease (e.g., ESA prohibitions) and how substitutes will function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Delisting Monitoring (PDM) statutory requirement and plan content
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4(g)(1) of the Act requires a monitoring program for not less than 5 years for species delisted due to recovery. The PDM plan should: (1) summarize status at delisting; (2) describe frequency and duration of monitoring; (3) discuss monitoring methods and sampling regimes; (4) define potential triggers for additional monitoring; (5) outline reporting requirements and procedures; (6) propose an implementation schedule; and (7) define responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalize PDM after addressing public comments; establish baseline densities/metrics and sampling protocols; specify triggers and actions if declines are detected (including potential reinstatement/listing procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: PDM triggers and restoration of protections
rubrics_metrics.description: If monitoring during the PDM period indicates a decline such that protective status under the Act should be reinstated, the Service can initiate listing procedures, including emergency listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define specific quantitative or qualitative triggers in the PDM plan and outline the process/timeline for responding to trigger events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant Portion of Its Range (SPOR) analysis approach
rubrics_metrics.description: For SPOR analysis, determine whether (1) a portion is 'significant' and (2) the species is endangered or threatened in that portion; the Service may address either question first and need not evaluate the second if the first is answered negatively. Focus on biologically meaningful portions where status might differ (consider distribution of individuals, threats, and resiliency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define how the range is partitioned, identify portions with different threat intensity or biological status, and explain why any portion is or is not biologically meaningful for significance/status determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to follow Administrative Procedure Act rulemaking process
rubrics_metrics.description: Delisting is accomplished only by issuing a rule through the Administrative Procedure Act rulemaking process (5 U.S.C. 551 et seq.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish proposed and final rules in the Federal Register, provide public notice and comment periods, respond to substantive comments in the final rule, and set an effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice, comment consideration, and response obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service must invite and consider written public comments on proposed rules; substantive information received must be incorporated into the final determination or addressed in the responses to comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document outreach (agency contacts, press releases, newspaper notices), maintain the docket on regulations.gov, summarize comments and the Service’s responses, and modify analyses or plans (e.g., PDM) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and availability of supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the rule and supporting documents (references cited, 5-year review, recovery outline, SSA report, PDM plan, datasets, technical notes) available to the public (e.g., regulations.gov docket).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide access to the SSA, peer review comments, monitoring data, technical reports, and literature cited; cite documents in the rule and provide instructions for obtaining materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-to-government consultation with Tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Presidential memoranda, EO 13175, Uniform Standards for Tribal Consultation, and Departmental guidance, the Service must communicate meaningfully with federally recognized Tribes on a government-to-government basis and consider tribal concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify affected Tribes, solicit comment, document consultation efforts, and incorporate Tribal input where received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of species' biological characteristics in vulnerability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate species' life-history and ecological traits (e.g., habitat generalist/specialist status, dispersal capability, longevity, recruitment and survivorship patterns) when assessing vulnerability to threats and climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use biological traits to interpret model outputs and plausibility of persistence under future scenarios (e.g., a habitat generalist may have lower climate vulnerability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effects analysis of delisting
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess and state the regulatory effects of delisting (e.g., removal from 50 CFR 17.12(h), cessation of ESA section 7 consultation obligations and section 9 prohibitions, no change if no critical habitat designated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state the date prohibitions and consultation obligations cease and any continuing protections under other laws or designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for relying on agency and partner conservation measures post-delisting
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on conservation actions implemented by other agencies (e.g., BLM ACECs, land management terms), evaluate whether those measures will continue, their likely effectiveness, and whether they sufficiently ameliorate threats in the absence of ESA protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific measures (avoidance buffers, special designations, permit terms), their expected persistence post-delisting, and incorporate them into future-condition analyses; acknowledge where protections will change (e.g., buffer reductions) and discuss implications.
